patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient has been experiencing tingling pain in the sole of his right foot for the last 6 weeks, which occurs when he raises his foot above chest level during exercises. He started exercising regularly 2 months ago and notices his right calf cramps when using the incline feature on his treadmill, requiring him to stop frequently. The pain subsides after a few minutes of rest. He has been managing type 2 diabetes mellitus for 8 years. He is a smoker with a 34-year history of smoking two packs per day.

Symptoms.Primary_Symptom: Tingling pain in the sole of the right foot during exercise
Secondary_Symptoms: Right calf cramps with incline exercise

patient_actor_hidden.Past_Medical_History: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, managed with metformin for the past 8 years.
patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Smoking history of two packs per day for 34 years.

objective_for_doctor: Evaluate a 55-year-old man presenting with foot pain and cramping during exercise, and diagnose the underlying condition.

turns.doctor_opening: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on?
turns.patient_opening: “Over the last 6 weeks I’ve had a tingling pain in the sole of my right foot whenever I lift that foot above chest level during exercise. Also, when I use the incline on the treadmill I get cramps in my right calf and have to stop, but the pain eases after a few minutes of rest.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any swelling in your joints?
turns.patient_answer: “Not really—no joint swelling that I’ve noticed. It’s mainly the tingling in the sole of my right foot when I elevate my foot during exercise, and the calf cramps with incline that ease after I rest.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any bumps, sores, or unusual growths on your scalp?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any bumps, sores, or unusual growths on my scalp.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been experiencing any itching or a persistent urge to scratch anywhere on your body?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had any itching or any persistent urge to scratch anywhere on my body.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you had any trouble lifting your arms above your head?
turns.patient_answer: “Not really—I'm able to lift my arms overhead without any particular trouble; it’s mainly in my right foot and calf during exercise.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any loss of vision that isn’t accompanied by pain?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had any loss of vision—no changes like that at all. It’s been localized to the tingling in the sole of my right foot during exercise and the calf cramps when I use the incline.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you had a fever that’s felt extremely hot—like a temperature above 104 °F (40 °C) that’s made you feel dizzy or very uncomfortable?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had any fever or felt extremely hot—no dizziness or feeling very uncomfortable like that. It’s really just the tingling in my right foot with lifting it during exercise and the right calf cramps on the incline that improve after I rest.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling unusually stressed or overwhelmed lately?
turns.patient_answer: “I wouldn’t say I’ve been unusually stressed or overwhelmed lately. It’s mainly that tingling in the sole of my right foot during exercise and the right calf cramps when I use the incline, and they improve after I rest.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you experienced any burning or discomfort when you urinate?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any burning or discomfort when I urinate.” “It’s been mainly the tingling in the sole of my right foot when I lift it above chest level during exercise, and the calf cramps on the treadmill incline that get better after I rest.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling chills lately?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had chills or any feverish feelings—nothing like that. It’s mainly just the tingling in the sole of my right foot when I lift that foot during exercise, and the right calf cramps on the treadmill incline that ease after a few minutes of rest.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any lumps or masses in your breast that feel fixed and don’t move when you touch them?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any lumps or masses in my breast—nothing that feels fixed or doesn’t move when I touch it.” “This has been mainly the tingling in the sole of my right foot during exercise and the calf cramps with incline that ease after a few minutes of rest.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling any pain or discomfort on the side of your back or abdomen, between your ribs and hips?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had any pain or discomfort on my back or abdomen between my ribs and hips—this has been mainly in my right foot when I lift it during exercise, and the right calf cramps with the treadmill incline that improve after a few minutes of rest.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel pain in your calf when you walk, and does that pain go away when you stop and rest?
turns.patient_answer: “Yes, I do get cramping pain in my right calf with walking on the treadmill when I use the incline, and it does go away after I stop and rest for a few minutes.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed that your urine looks darker than usual?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed my urine looking darker than usual—I haven’t had any changes to it that stood out. It’s been pretty much the tingling in the sole of my right foot and the right calf cramps with the treadmill incline that ease after I rest.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you find it hard to lift your arm above your head or reach across your body?
turns.patient_answer: “Not really—I'm able to lift my arms overhead and reach across my body without any trouble. The problems are mainly in my right foot with that tingling and the right calf cramps during incline exercise that improve after I rest.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been using the same joints repeatedly—like typing, playing an instrument, or doing manual work—and noticed any pain or stiffness from it?
turns.patient_answer: “No, it doesn’t seem linked to using one particular joint repeatedly like typing or manual work. It’s more consistent with exercise—when I lift my right foot above chest level I get tingling in the sole, and with treadmill incline I get right calf cramps that stop after a few minutes of rest.”
